questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Angle Pairs Along Corridors
questions.content_markdown:
In the telemetry diagram below, orbital lines $a$ and $b$ are parallel ($a \parallel b$). Transversal $c$ forms alternate interior angle $\widehat{A_3} = 62^\circ$. What is the degree measure of alternate interior angle $\widehat{B_1}$?

![Figure: Alternate Interior Angles](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q1.svg)
questions.explanation: Since line $a \parallel b$, alternate interior angles are equal in measure: $\widehat{B_1} = \widehat{A_3} = 62^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Angle Pairs Along Corridors
questions.content_markdown:
Parallel flight corridors $m \parallel n$ are intersected by navigation vector $t$. If corresponding angle $\widehat{M_1} = 118^\circ$ (top-right), what is the measure of corresponding angle $\widehat{N_1}$ (top-right)?

![Figure: Corresponding Angles](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q2.svg)
questions.explanation: Because lines $m \parallel n$, corresponding angles occupying the same relative position are equal: $\widehat{N_1} = \widehat{M_1} = 118^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Angle Pairs Along Corridors
questions.content_markdown:
Communication lines $p \parallel q$ are cut by transversal $k$. Given that consecutive interior angle $\widehat{P_4} = 74^\circ$, calculate the degree measure of consecutive interior angle $\widehat{Q_1}$.

![Figure: Consecutive Interior Angles](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q3.svg)
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles along parallel lines are supplementary: $\widehat{Q_1} = 180^\circ - \widehat{P_4} = 180^\circ - 74^\circ = 106^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Varied Orientations & Transversals
questions.content_markdown:
Two vertical sensor towers represented by parallel lines $x \parallel y$ are crossed by scanning beam $d$. If angle $\widehat{X_1} = 55^\circ$, what is the measure of alternate interior angle $\widehat{Y_2}$?

![Figure: Vertical Parallel Lines](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q4.svg)
questions.explanation: Even when parallel lines are oriented vertically, the alternate interior angle theorem holds: $\widehat{Y_2} = \widehat{X_1} = 55^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Varied Orientations & Transversals
questions.content_markdown:
Tilted solar panel rails $r \parallel s$ are crossed by horizontal support beam $h$. If corresponding angle $\alpha = 135^\circ$, what is the measure of corresponding angle $\beta$ on rail $s$?

![Figure: Tilted Parallel Lines](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q5.svg)
questions.explanation: Parallel lines $r \parallel s$ cut by horizontal transversal $h$ have equal corresponding angles: $\beta = \alpha = 135^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 2: Venus Base • Varied Orientations & Transversals
questions.content_markdown:
Look at the diagram below. Lines $a$ and $b$ are parallel ($a \parallel b$). If the acute angle at node $A$ is $70^\circ$, find the measure of consecutive interior angle $\theta$.

![Figure: Steep Transversal Angle](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q6.svg)
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary: $\theta = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Finding Unknown Angles & Linear Pairs
questions.content_markdown:
Corridors $a \parallel b$ are cut by transversal $c$. Given exterior angle $\widehat{A_1} = 125^\circ$, calculate acute interior angle $\widehat{B_2}$.

![Figure: Exterior to Interior Conversion](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q7.svg)
questions.explanation: Corresponding angle $\widehat{B_1} = \widehat{A_1} = 125^\circ$. Since $\widehat{B_1}$ and $\widehat{B_2}$ form a linear pair along line $b$: $\widehat{B_2} = 180^\circ - 125^\circ = 55^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Finding Unknown Angles & Linear Pairs
questions.content_markdown:
In the orbital grid, $m \parallel n$. Given that angle $\widehat{M_4} = 48^\circ$, determine the degree measure of angle $\widehat{N_2}$.

![Figure: Vertical and Corresponding](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q8.svg)
questions.explanation: At node $M$, vertically opposite angle $\widehat{M_2} = \widehat{M_4} = 48^\circ$. Since $m \parallel n$, corresponding angle $\widehat{N_2} = \widehat{M_2} = 48^circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Finding Unknown Angles & Linear Pairs
questions.content_markdown:
Trajectories $p \parallel q$ are intersected by flight path $s$. If $\widehat{P_2} = 142^\circ$, what is the measure of angle $\widehat{Q_3}$?

![Figure: Two Intersection Transfer](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q9.svg)
questions.explanation: Corresponding angle $\widehat{Q_2} = \widehat{P_2} = 142^\circ$. Angle $\widehat{Q_3}$ and $\widehat{Q_2}$ are vertically opposite, so $\widehat{Q_3} = 142^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Finding Unknown Angles & Linear Pairs
questions.content_markdown:
Given $a \parallel b$ cut by transversal $c$. If angle $\widehat{A_2} = 135^\circ$ (top-left), what is the degree measure of angle $\widehat{B_4}$ (bottom-right)?

![Figure: Diagonal Corner Angle](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q10.svg)
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angle to $\widehat{A_2}$ is $180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ$. The vertically opposite angle $\widehat{B_4} = 45^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Algebraic Expressions with x
questions.content_markdown:
In the diagram, corridors $a$ and $b$ are parallel ($a \parallel b$). Alternate interior angles measure $(2x + 15)^\circ$ and $65^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.

![Figure: Algebraic Alternate Interior](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q11.svg)
questions.explanation: Since $a \parallel b$, alternate interior angles are equal: $2x + 15 = 65 \implies 2x = 50 \implies x = 25$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Algebraic Expressions with x
questions.content_markdown:
Given parallel lines $m \parallel n$. Two corresponding angles are given as $(3x - 10)^\circ$ and $80^\circ$. Calculate $x$.

![Figure: Algebraic Corresponding Angles](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q12.svg)
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal: $3x - 10 = 80 \implies 3x = 90 \implies x = 30$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 4: Mars Outpost • Algebraic Expressions with x
questions.content_markdown:
Along parallel flight corridors $p \parallel q$, consecutive interior angles measure $(2x + 20)^\circ$ and $(x + 40)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.

![Figure: Supplementary Algebraic Equation](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q13.svg)
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary: $(2x + 20) + (x + 40) = 180 \implies 3x + 60 = 180 \implies 3x = 120 \implies x = 40$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Perpendicular to Parallel & Right Angles
questions.content_markdown:
Docking struts $a$ and $b$ are both perpendicular to base mast $c$ ($a \perp c$ and $b \perp c$). Diagonal sensor beam $d$ crosses strut $a$ at an acute angle of $52^\circ$. What is the measure of the alternate interior angle on strut $b$?

![Figure: Double Perpendicular and Transversal](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q14.svg)
questions.explanation: Since $a \perp c$ and $b \perp c$, struts $a$ and $b$ are parallel ($a \parallel b$ by Theorem 1). Therefore, alternate interior angles formed by diagonal beam $d$ are equal: $52^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Perpendicular to Parallel & Right Angles
questions.content_markdown:
Corridors $a$ and $b$ are parallel ($a \parallel b$). Laser line $c$ is perpendicular to corridor $a$ ($c \perp a$). A probe trajectory $d$ passes through point $A$ making an angle of $34^\circ$ with line $c$. Find the complementary angle between probe trajectory $d$ and corridor $a$.

![Figure: Perpendicular with Trajectory](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q15.svg)
questions.explanation: Since $c \perp a$, the total angle is $90^\circ$. The complementary angle is $90^\circ - 34^\circ = 56^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 5: Jupiter Station • Perpendicular to Parallel & Right Angles
questions.content_markdown:
Parallel corridors $a \parallel b$ are connected by perpendicular strut $AB$ ($AB \perp b$ at $B$). Diagonal brace $AC$ connects node $A$ on line $a$ to node $C$ on line $b$. If $\widehat{BAC} = 32^\circ$, what is the measure of angle $\widehat{ACB}$ in triangle $ABC$?

![Figure: Right Triangle Between Parallels](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q16.svg)
questions.explanation: In right triangle $ABC$ with $\widehat{B} = 90^\circ$, the two acute angles are complementary: $\widehat{ACB} = 90^\circ - 32^\circ = 58^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Angle Bisectors on Parallel Lines
questions.content_markdown:
Corridors $a \parallel b$ are intersected by transversal line $AB$. Angle $\widehat{A_3} = 70^\circ$. Ray $AT$ bisects angle $\widehat{A_3}$ and meets line $b$ at point $T$. What is the measure of angle $\widehat{ATB}$?

![Figure: Angle Bisector Transversal](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q17.svg)
questions.explanation: The bisector divides $70^\circ$ into two $35^\circ$ angles. Between parallel lines $a \parallel b$ cut by transversal $AT$, alternate interior angle $\widehat{ATB}$ equals the upper half-angle: $\widehat{ATB} = 35^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Angle Bisectors on Parallel Lines
questions.content_markdown:
Parallel corridors $a \parallel b$ have consecutive interior angles at nodes $A$ and $B$. The angle bisectors of these two consecutive interior angles intersect at point $P$. What is ALWAYS the measure of angle $\widehat{APB}$?

![Figure: Perpendicular Bisector Intersection](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q18.svg)
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles sum to $180^\circ$. Their bisectors take half of each, so $\widehat{PAB} + \widehat{PBA} = 180^\circ \div 2 = 90^\circ$. In triangle $APB$, the third angle is $\widehat{APB} = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 6: Saturn Rings • Angle Bisectors on Parallel Lines
questions.content_markdown:
Transversal $AB$ cuts parallel lines $a \parallel b$. Ray $Ax$ bisects alternate interior angle $\widehat{A_3} = 80^\circ$, and ray $By$ bisects alternate interior angle $\widehat{B_1} = 80^\circ$. What is the geometric relationship between ray $Ax$ and ray $By$?

![Figure: Alternate Interior Bisectors](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q19.svg)
questions.explanation: The half-angles each measure $40^\circ$. Because these equal half-angles are alternate interior angles for rays $Ax$ and $By$ cut by transversal $AB$, ray $Ax$ is parallel to ray $By$ ($Ax \parallel By$).

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • The Zig-Zag / Auxiliary Ray Problems
questions.content_markdown:
In deep space navigation, ray $Ax \parallel \text{Ray } By$. Waypoint $O$ lies between the rays such that acute angles $\widehat{xAO} = 35^\circ$ and $\widehat{yBO} = 45^\circ$. Calculate corner deflection angle $\widehat{AOB}$.

![Figure: Acute Zig-Zag Ray](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q20.svg)
questions.explanation: Draw auxiliary ray $Ot \parallel Ax \parallel By$. Alternate interior angles give $\widehat{AOt} = 35^\circ$ and $\widehat{tOB} = 45^\circ$. Thus $\widehat{AOB} = 35^\circ + 45^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • The Zig-Zag / Auxiliary Ray Problems
questions.content_markdown:
Look at the orbital trajectory diagram below. Ray $Ax \parallel \text{Ray } By$. Given that $\widehat{OAx} = 50^\circ$ and $\widehat{OBy} = 60^\circ$, find the measure of angle $\widehat{AOB}$.

![Figure: Reflex Zig-Zag Corridor](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q21.svg)
questions.explanation: By drawing auxiliary line $Ot \parallel Ax \parallel By$, angle $\widehat{AOB}$ is the sum of the two alternate interior angles: $50^\circ + 60^circ = 110^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • The Zig-Zag / Auxiliary Ray Problems
questions.content_markdown:
Refer to the diagram below. Ray $Ax \parallel \text{Ray } By$. Inside the corridor, obtuse angles measure $\widehat{xAO} = 130^\circ$ and $\widehat{yBO} = 150^\circ$. Calculate the interior angle $\widehat{AOB}$.

![Figure: Obtuse Zig-Zag Angles](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q22.svg)
questions.explanation: Draw auxiliary ray $Ot \parallel Ax \parallel By$ directed right. Consecutive interior angles on the same side sum to $180^\circ$: $\widehat{AOt} = 180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ$ and $\widehat{tOB} = 180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ$. Therefore, $\widehat{AOB} = 50^\circ + 30^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 8: Neptune Frontier • Multi-Line Systems & Complex Synthesis
questions.content_markdown:
Three orbital corridors are parallel: $a \parallel b \parallel c$. Transversal line $d$ crosses line $a$ at an acute angle of $68^\circ$. What is the measure of the corresponding angle formed by line $d$ with line $c$?

![Figure: Three Parallel Lines Transversal](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q23.svg)
questions.explanation: By transitivity, $a \parallel c$. Therefore, transversal $d$ forms equal corresponding angles on lines $a$ and $c$, so the angle is $68^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 8: Neptune Frontier • Multi-Line Systems & Complex Synthesis
questions.content_markdown:
Parallel flight tracks $a \parallel b$ are crossed by two flight paths that intersect at point $K$ between the tracks. If $\widehat{KAB} = 45^\circ$ and $\widehat{KBA} = 65^\circ$, what is the measure of alternate interior angle $\widehat{KDC}$ on line $b$?

![Figure: Intersecting Transversals in Parallel Tracks](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q24.svg)
questions.explanation: Segment $BD$ is a transversal crossing parallel lines $a \parallel b$. Angle $\widehat{KBA}$ and angle $\widehat{KDC}$ are alternate interior angles, so $\widehat{KDC} = \widehat{KBA} = 65^\circ$.

questions.sectionName: Sector 8: Neptune Frontier • Multi-Line Systems & Complex Synthesis
questions.content_markdown:
In a multi-leg space corridor, ray $Ax \parallel \text{Ray } Cy$. The flight path bends at waypoints $O$ and $P$. Given that $\widehat{xAO} = 30^\circ$, $\widehat{AOP} = 80^\circ$, and $\widehat{OPC} = 70^\circ$, determine the measure of navigation angle $\widehat{PCy}$.

![Figure: Stepped Double Zig-Zag Corridor](/images/geometry/math7_l10_q25.svg)
questions.explanation: Draw auxiliary ray $Ot \parallel Ax$: alternate interior angle gives $\widehat{AOt} = 30^\circ \implies \widehat{tOP} = 80^\circ - 30^\circ = 50^\circ$. Draw auxiliary ray $Pu \parallel Ot \parallel Ax$: alternate interior angle gives $\widehat{OPu} = 50^\circ \implies \widehat{uPC} = 70^\circ - 50^\circ = 20^\circ$. Since $Pu \parallel Cy$, alternate interior angle $\widehat{PCy} = 20^\circ$.
